Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a single handcrafted crochet product available in The Crochet Studio's inventory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

description.description: A detailed description of the product, including materials, size, and unique features.

price.description: The selling price of the product.

category.description: The category the product belongs to (e.g., 'bags', 'toys', 'clothes').

stockQuantity.description: The current quantity of the product available in stock.

imageUrls.description: An array of URLs pointing to images of the product, stored in Firebase Storage.

tags.description: An optional array of descriptive tags associated with the product (e.g., 'winter', 'gift', 'handmade').

isFeatured.description: A boolean indicating if the product should be prominently displayed in featured sections on the website.

isPublished.description: A boolean indicating if the product is visible and available for purchase on the public website.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the product was first created in the system.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the product's information was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual product details for The Crochet Studio. Documents include `id`, `name`, `description`, `price`, `category`, `stockQuantity`, `imageUrls` (array of Firebase Storage URLs), `tags` (optional array), `isFeatured`, `isPublished`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt` timestamps. Public users can read documents where `isPublished` is true. Authenticated admin users (as defined in `/admin_users`) have full read, write, update, and delete access to all product documents.

params.name: productId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific product document.

definition.description: This collection serves as a marker for administrative privileges. Each document's ID (`adminId`) is the Firebase Authentication UID of a user who possesses admin rights. The existence of a document at `/admin_users/{request.auth.uid}` is used by Firestore Security Rules to grant administrative access (read, write, update, delete) to protected collections like `/products`. This implements the DBAC (Database Access Control) strategy and ensures Authorization Independence by denormalizing role information into a top-level collection.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The Firebase Authentication User ID (UID) of an admin user.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, adhering to all specified core design principles and mandates. 

**Authorization Independence:** To achieve authorization independence, the critical principle, we introduce a top-level collection `/admin_users/{adminId}`. This collection stores marker documents where each document's ID is the Firebase Authentication UID of an admin user. Firebase Security Rules will use an `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/admin_users/$(request.auth.uid))` check to determine if the requesting user has admin privileges. This approach completely eliminates the need for `get()` calls to parent documents or within the product document itself for authorization, ensuring atomic operations and simplifying rule debugging.

**QAPs (Queries as Permissions) and Structural Segregation:** The main collection for product data is `/products/{productId}`. This collection will store all product documents, regardless of their publication status. The `Product` entity includes an `isPublished` boolean field. This field is central to enabling secure `list` operations (QAPs) and managing heterogeneous read access within a single collection without violating structural segregation principles.
*   **Public Read Access:** Public users (unauthenticated) will only be able to read documents where `isPublished` is explicitly `true`. A query like `db.collection('products').where('isPublished', '==', true)` will work securely and efficiently. The security rules will enforce this, preventing public users from accessing unpublished products.
*   **Admin Read Access:** Authenticated admin users, identified by their UID existing in the `/admin_users` collection, will have full read access to all documents in `/products`, regardless of their `isPublished` status. This allows the admin panel to display all products, including drafts or unpublished items.
*   **Write/Update/Delete Access:** All write, update, and delete operations on the `/products` collection are strictly restricted to authenticated admin users, as enforced by security rules checking against the `/admin_users` collection.

This design ensures that authorization logic is clear, external to the primary data documents where possible (for roles), and supports efficient, secure querying for both public-facing applications and the admin panel.
